headline: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
summary: Google's new unified agent for Gemini can take ownership of tasks, plan work, and connect to internal business systems, initially rolling out to enterprise users. This moves AI beyond just conversational experiences.
details: Google announced a unified agent for Gemini that moves beyond answering questions to getting tasks done on the user's behalf. This agent can plan work, use custom skills, and connect to internal business systems from a single interface.

The shift reflects a broader trend in AI, where tools are evolving from conversational experiences to taking ownership of assigned tasks. This includes generating code, scheduling meetings, and booking travel.
Google CEO Sundar Pichai highlighted Gemini's significant reach, with over 1 billion monthly active users. Nearly 90% of Fortune 100 businesses currently utilize Gemini Enterprise.

The agent will first be rolled out to businesses, addressing "harder problems around security, scale, and performance." This strategic approach aims to refine the powerful agents before a wider consumer release.

According to Google Cloud CEO Thomas Kurian, the new agent can be given "objectives, not just instructions." It can autonomously plan tasks, leverage custom skills and tools, and integrate with a business's internal systems.

Users can choose the best model for a task, with the AI defaulting to an optimal choice. The system supports third-party models, starting with Anthropic's Claude, and plans to expand to open-source and private models.

The agent handles attachments like files and folders and connects securely to various business data and systems. This includes Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, Slack, Jira, Confluence, Git, BigQuery, and more.
A "tasks inbox" interface allows users to monitor Gemini's progress, view its thought process, and observe task delegation to subagents. It also shows the loading of special skills and code.
Notably, the AI will operate with its own Workspace account, complete with an email address and contextual awareness. It understands company structure, time zones, approval workflows, and calendars.

Users can interact with the agent by tagging it, emailing it, sharing content, or adding it to group chats. All actions taken by the agent are recorded in an audit trail attributed to the AI, not a person.

The agent will be accessible across multiple platforms, including iOS and Android mobile devices, Windows and Mac desktops, and via command line interface. It also integrates with Google Workspace, Microsoft 365, ServiceNow, and Slack.

Early testers included sportswear brand On, Shopify, and PayPal, with major enterprise customers like BNP Paribas and Merck already using Gemini Enterprise. Google also introduced flexible spending options to help businesses manage AI costs.
